zones.label: Virginia marine waters
zones.bagNote: No bag limit

Not the same fish as king mackerel, which has a 27 inch minimum and 3 per person.

Check the SAFMC/NOAA dolphin page for the current size and bag limit before keeping fish.

species.name: Sharks (large coastal group)
species.quote: E. It shall be unlawful for any person to take, harvest, land, or possess any blacktip, bull, great hammerhead, lemon, nurse, scalloped hammerhead, smooth hammerhead, spinner or tiger shark from May 15 through July 15 of any calendar year. ... D. ... less than 54 inches in fork length ... 1. ... great hammerhead, scalloped hammerhead, or smooth hammerhead shark that is less than 78 inches in fork length. ... A. Recreational fishing vessels are allowed a maximum possession limit of one recreationally permitted shark, excluding smooth dogfish, per trip, regardless of the number of people on board the vessel.
species.size: 54 inches fork length; hammerheads 78 inches fork length
species.limit: 1 per vessel per trip (shore angler: 1 per calendar day)
species.notes: Must be landed with head, tail and fins attached; handline or rod and reel only; non-offset corrodible non-stainless circle hooks required except with flies or artificial lures; spearing and bowfishing illegal.

zones.label: Virginia marine waters (to 3 mi)
zones.bagNote: 1 recreationally permitted shark per vessel per trip (a non-boat shore angler gets the vessel limit per day)
zones.sizeNote: 54 inch fork length minimum; great, scalloped and smooth hammerhead 78 inch fork length minimum

userNotes: Closed May 15 through July 15 every year for blacktip, bull, great/scalloped/smooth hammerhead, lemon, nurse, spinner and tiger sharks.
The 1-per-vessel limit covers ALL permitted sharks on the boat combined (except bonnethead, Atlantic sharpnose and smooth dogfish), no matter how many anglers are aboard.
Hammerheads must be 78 inches fork length; all others in this group 54 inches fork length.
Land sharks whole: head, tail and fins attached. Rod and reel or handline only; circle hooks required with bait.
Federal waters beyond 3 miles follow NMFS HMS rules, which differ.

species.name: Atlantic Sharpnose Shark
species.quote: In addition, each recreational vessel angler may possess one bonnethead and one Atlantic sharpnose per trip. ... 2. Atlantic sharpnose, bonnethead, finetooth, blacknose, and smooth dogfish sharks are exempt from the recreational size limit described in this subsection.
species.limit: 1 per person per trip (vessel) or per calendar day (shore)
species.notes: In addition to the 1-per-vessel limit on other sharks. Head, tail and fins attached; rod and reel or handline only; circle hooks with bait.

zones.label: Virginia marine waters (to 3 mi)
zones.bagNote: 1 per person, in addition to the vessel's 1 other permitted shark

userNotes: Each angler may keep 1 Atlantic sharpnose AND 1 bonnethead per trip, on top of the boat's single other permitted shark.
No minimum size. Land whole with head, tail and fins attached.

species.name: Bonnethead Shark
species.quote: In addition, each recreational vessel angler may possess one bonnethead and one Atlantic sharpnose per trip. ... 2. Atlantic sharpnose, bonnethead, finetooth, blacknose, and smooth dogfish sharks are exempt from the recreational size limit described in this subsection.
species.limit: 1 per person per trip (vessel) or per calendar day (shore)
species.notes: In addition to the 1-per-vessel limit on other sharks. Head, tail and fins attached; rod and reel or handline only; circle hooks with bait.

zones.label: Virginia marine waters (to 3 mi)
zones.bagNote: 1 per person, in addition to the vessel's 1 other permitted shark

userNotes: Each angler may keep 1 bonnethead AND 1 Atlantic sharpnose per trip, on top of the boat's single other permitted shark.
No minimum size. Land whole with head, tail and fins attached.

species.name: Sharks (blacknose & finetooth)
species.quote: 2. Atlantic sharpnose, bonnethead, finetooth, blacknose, and smooth dogfish sharks are exempt from the recreational size limit described in this subsection. ... A. Recreational fishing vessels are allowed a maximum possession limit of one recreationally permitted shark, excluding smooth dogfish, per trip
species.limit: 1 per vessel per trip (counts as the vessel's one permitted shark)
species.notes: No minimum size but still count toward the 1-per-vessel permitted shark limit. Head, tail and fins attached; rod and reel or handline only.

zones.label: Virginia marine waters (to 3 mi)
zones.bagNote: 1 per vessel per trip (shares the single-shark vessel limit with the large coastal and pelagic groups)

userNotes: Blacknose and finetooth have no minimum size, but a boat may keep only ONE permitted shark total (other than sharpnose, bonnethead and smooth dogfish).
Not subject to the May 15 - July 15 large coastal closure.

species.name: Sharks (pelagic: blue, porbeagle, thresher)
species.quote: "Recreationally permitted shark" means any of the following species: ... Blue, Prionace glauca ... Porbeagle, Lamna nasus ... Thresher, Alopias vulpinus
species.notes: Permitted species not in the May 15 - July 15 closure group. Size and vessel limit from 4VAC20-490-40 D and A. Head, tail and fins attached; rod and reel or handline only.

zones.label: Virginia marine waters (to 3 mi)
zones.bagNote: 1 per vessel per trip (shares the single-shark vessel limit)

userNotes: Blue, porbeagle and common thresher are recreationally permitted year-round at 54 inches fork length, 1 per vessel.
Bigeye thresher, shortfin mako and longfin mako are PROHIBITED - do not confuse them with common thresher.
Federal waters beyond 3 miles follow NMFS HMS rules.

species.name: Dogfish (smooth & spiny)
species.quote: No size or possession limits apply to Dog Sharks. ... All sharks (All species except Spiny Dog Sharks) must be landed with head and fins attached
species.notes: Smooth dogfish must still be landed with head and fins attached; spiny dogfish are exempt from that rule.

zones.label: Virginia marine waters (to 3 mi)
zones.bagNote: No size or possession limit

userNotes: No size or bag limit on smooth or spiny dogfish.
Smooth dogfish must be landed whole (head and fins attached); spiny dogfish are exempt from the head-and-fins rule.
Dogfish do not count toward the 1-per-vessel shark limit.

species.name: Sharks (recreationally prohibited)
species.quote: "Recreationally prohibited shark" means any of the following species: Atlantic angel, Squatina dumeril; Basking, Cetorhinus maximus; Bigeye sand tiger, Odontaspis noronhai; Bigeye sixgill, Hexanchus nakamurai; Bigeye thresher, Alopias superciliosus; Bignose, Carcharhinus altimus; Caribbean reef, Carcharhinus perezii; Caribbean sharpnose, Rhizoprionodon porosus; Dusky, Carcharhinus obscurus; Galapagos, Carcharhinus galapagensis; Longfin mako, Isurus paucus; Narrowtooth, Carcharhinus brachyurus; Night, Carcharhinus signatus; Oceanic whitetip, Carcharhinus longimanus; Sand tiger, Carcharias taurus; Sandbar, Carcharhinus plumbeus; Sevengill, Heptranchias perlo; Shortfin mako, Isurus oxyrinchus; Silky, Carcharhinus falciformis; Sixgill, Hexanchus griseus; Smalltail, Carcharhinus porosus; Whale, Rhincodon typus; White, Carcharodon carcharias
species.notes: 4VAC20-490-40 C: It shall be unlawful for any person to possess any recreationally prohibited shark.

zones.label: Virginia marine waters (to 3 mi)
zones.bagNote: Possession prohibited

userNotes: These 23 species may not be taken or possessed recreationally in Virginia. Most commonly encountered: sandbar, dusky, sand tiger, Atlantic angel, white, bigeye thresher and both makos.
Shortfin and longfin mako were added to the prohibited list (regulation amended May 2025); the MRC web table footnote about mako sizes is outdated.

species.name: American Lobster
species.quote: It shall be unlawful for any person to possess any lobster less than 3-17/32 inches in carapace length or any lobster greater than 5-1/4 inches in carapace length ... E. It shall be unlawful to land lobster from February 1 through March 31. ... A. It shall be unlawful for any person to possess any berried female lobster ... C. ... to possess a V-notched female lobster. D. It shall be unlawful to possess a lobster that has an outer shell that has been speared.
species.notes: No berried (egg-bearing) or V-notched females; no speared lobsters; no detached tails, claws or meat aboard a vessel.

zones.label: Virginia marine waters
zones.bagNote: No recreational possession limit printed in 4VAC20-110
zones.sizeNote: Carapace length 3-17/32 inch minimum, 5-1/4 inch maximum

userNotes: Measure carapace length: keep only 3-17/32 to 5-1/4 inches.
No landing of lobster February 1 through March 31.
Release egg-bearing and V-notched females; spearing lobsters is illegal; keep them whole on the boat.

species.name: Hybrid Striped Bass
aliases: striped bass x white bass hybrid
species.quote: Striped Bass - Landlocked Striped Bass and Landlocked Striped Bass X White Bass Hybrids ... 4 per day in the aggregate No fish less than 20 inches
species.limit: 4 per day in the aggregate (striped bass and hybrids combined)
species.notes: Lake exceptions: Buggs Island/Kerr (Oct 1-May 31: 2/day aggregate, 20-26 inch slot; Jun 1-Sep 30: 4/day no length limit); Claytor Lake (Sep 16-Jun 30: 2/day, 20 inch min; Jul 1-Sep 15: 4/day no length limit); Lake Gaston (4/day; Oct 1-May 31 20 inch min; Jun 1-Sep 30 no length limit); Smith Mountain Lake (2/day; Nov 1-May 31 no fish 30-40 inches; Jun 1-Oct 31 no length limit).

zones.label: Virginia inland waters (statewide)
zones.bagNote: 4 per day, striped bass and hybrids combined

zones.label: Buggs Island Lake/Kerr Reservoir incl. Staunton River to Leesville Dam and Dan River to Union St. Dam
zones.bagNote: Oct 1-May 31: 2 per day aggregate (20-26 inch slot); Jun 1-Sep 30: 4 per day aggregate, no length limit
zones.sizeNote: Oct 1-May 31: 20 to 26 inch slot; Jun 1-Sep 30: none

zones.label: Claytor Lake and tributaries
zones.bagNote: Sep 16-Jun 30: 2 per day aggregate, 20 inch min; Jul 1-Sep 15: 4 per day aggregate, no length limit

zones.label: Lake Gaston
zones.bagNote: 4 per day aggregate

zones.label: Smith Mountain Lake and tributaries incl. Roanoke River to Niagara Dam
zones.bagNote: 2 per day aggregate
zones.sizeNote: Nov 1-May 31: no fish 30 to 40 inches; Jun 1-Oct 31: none

userNotes: Hybrids share one 4-fish aggregate with landlocked striped bass statewide (20 inch minimum).
Kerr, Claytor, Gaston and Smith Mountain Lake each have their own seasonal slot or minimum - check the zone for the lake you are on.

species.name: Roanoke Bass
species.quote: Roanoke Bass 25 per day in the aggregate with rock bass No statewide length limits | Nottoway, Meherrin, and Blackwater (Franklin County), Blackwater (Chowan), Falling and Smith rivers and their tributaries | 5 per day in the aggregate (combined) with rock bass No Roanoke bass less than 8 inches
species.limit: 25 per day in the aggregate with rock bass
species.notes: Nottoway, Meherrin, Blackwater (Franklin Co.), Blackwater (Chowan), Falling and Smith rivers and tributaries: 5 per day combined with rock bass, no Roanoke bass less than 8 inches.

zones.label: Virginia inland waters (statewide)
zones.bagNote: 25 per day, rock bass and Roanoke bass combined

zones.label: Nottoway, Meherrin, Blackwater (Franklin Co. and Chowan), Falling and Smith rivers and tributaries
zones.bagNote: 5 per day, rock bass and Roanoke bass combined

userNotes: Statewide: 25 per day combined with rock bass, no size limit.
In the Nottoway, Meherrin, Blackwater, Falling and Smith river systems: only 5 per day combined and an 8 inch minimum.

species.name: White Perch
species.quote: Perch (yellow and white) No statewide daily limit No statewide length limit | Lake Moomaw 10 per day
species.notes: Nongame page: white perch may be possessed in unlimited numbers; may also be taken below the fall line in tidal rivers with a gill net under VMRC recreational rules. Lake Moomaw exception printed for the perch row (10 per day).

zones.label: Virginia inland waters (statewide)
zones.bagNote: No daily limit

zones.label: Lake Moomaw
zones.bagNote: 10 per day

userNotes: No statewide limit on white perch.
Lake Moomaw: 10 perch per day.

species.name: Bowfin
species.quote: Bowfin July 1 to April 14: 5 per day April 15 to June 30: 1 per day No statewide length limits
species.limit: July 1 to April 14: 5 per day; April 15 to June 30: 1 per day
species.notes: Bow and arrow allowed in tidal waters (below fall line); bowfin taken by bow must be retained.

zones.label: Virginia inland waters (statewide)
zones.bagNote: 5 per day Jul 1 - Apr 14; 1 per day Apr 15 - Jun 30

userNotes: Spawning-season limit: only 1 per day from April 15 through June 30; 5 per day the rest of the year.
Printed as its own row by DWR, separate from longnose gar (same limits).

species.name: Grass Carp
species.quote: Grass Carp No statewide daily limit No statewide length limit | Anglers may possess grass carp taken from inland public waters, except for public lakes and reservoirs. Anglers must ensure that harvested grass carp are dead.
species.notes: May not be harvested from public lakes and reservoirs (Department-owned or controlled lakes). Must be killed; bow and arrow allowed except in trout-stocked waters; bow-taken fish must be retained.

zones.label: Virginia inland public rivers and streams (not public lakes/reservoirs)
zones.bagNote: No daily limit; harvested fish must be dead

userNotes: Legal to keep from public rivers and streams only - not from public lakes or reservoirs.
Every grass carp you keep must be dead before you leave the water.

species.name: Common Carp
species.quote: No possession limits - can be possessed in unlimited numbers. Carp, mullet, white sucker, northern hogsucker, gizzard shad, threadfin shad, white perch, yellow perch (10 fish limit in Lake Moomaw), alewife and blueback herring [see limits under Anadromous (coastal) in creel and length limits table], stoneroller (hornyhead), fathead minnow, golden shiner, goldfish, and Asian clams.
species.notes: Bow and arrow (including crossbow) allowed day and night except in trout-stocked waters; bow-taken carp must be retained and not returned to the water.

zones.label: Virginia inland waters
zones.bagNote: No possession limit

userNotes: No limit on common carp.
If taken by bow, the fish must be kept, not thrown back or dumped on the bank.

species.name: Nongame fish (no possession limit)
species.quote: No possession limits - can be possessed in unlimited numbers. Carp, mullet, white sucker, northern hogsucker, gizzard shad, threadfin shad, white perch, yellow perch (10 fish limit in Lake Moomaw), alewife and blueback herring [see limits under Anadromous (coastal) in creel and length limits table], stoneroller (hornyhead), fathead minnow, golden shiner, goldfish, and Asian clams.
species.notes: Gizzard shad and white perch may also be taken below the fall line in Chesapeake Bay tidal rivers by gill net under VMRC recreational rules. Alewife and blueback herring are NOT unlimited - see their own rows (possession banned in coastal rivers).

zones.label: Virginia inland waters
zones.bagNote: No possession limit

userNotes: DWR lists these nongame fish as unlimited: carp, mullet, white sucker, northern hogsucker, gizzard shad, threadfin shad, white perch, yellow perch, stoneroller, fathead minnow, golden shiner, goldfish, Asian clams.
Alewife and blueback herring are listed here but are closed in all Chesapeake Bay coastal rivers and the Chowan drainage - see those rows.

species.name: Other nongame fish (20 per day)
species.quote: Other native or naturalized nongame fish 20 per day No length limits | Statewide | See pages 27-28 for exceptions
species.notes: Nongame page: 20 - Nongame Fish and Aquatic Invertebrates (personal use). Suckers: 20 per day by dip net (Feb 15 - May 15) or snagging/gigging in listed waters. Bait minnows/chubs/hellgrammites: 50 in aggregate. Crayfish: 20 in aggregate. In designated stocked trout waters nongame fish may be taken only by hook and line Oct 1 - Jun 15.

zones.label: Virginia inland waters (statewide)
zones.bagNote: 20 per day

userNotes: Any native or naturalized nongame fish not listed as unlimited: 20 per day.
Bait minnows, chubs and hellgrammites: 50 combined unless you have a purchase receipt. Crayfish: 20 combined.
Suckers taken by dip net (Feb 15 - May 15) or by snagging/gigging in the listed southwest Virginia waters: 20 per day.

species.name: Threatened and endangered fish (no possession)
species.quote: Threatened and endangered species No possession | None apply | None apply
species.notes: Nongame page: No possession allowed. Threatened and endangered species, freshwater mussels, candy darter, eastern hellbender, diamondback terrapin, and spotted turtle. It shall be unlawful to take mussels from any inland waters in Virginia.

zones.label: Virginia inland waters
zones.bagNote: Possession prohibited

userNotes: No possession of any state or federally threatened or endangered species, freshwater mussels, candy darter or eastern hellbender.
Freshwater mussels may not be taken from any inland water in Virginia.

species.name: Hickory Shad
species.quote: Hickory Shad - Above and below the fall line in all coastal rivers of the Chesapeake Bay and their tributaries: Creel and length limits shall be the same as those set by the Virginia Marine Resources Comm. in tidal rivers | Meherrin River below Emporia Dam, Nottoway River, Blackwater River (Chowan Drainage), North Landing and Northwest rivers, and their tributaries plus Back Bay: 10 per day No length limits
species.size: No length limit (Chowan drainage); Chesapeake rivers as set by VMRC
species.limit: 10 per day in the Chowan drainage rivers; Chesapeake Bay coastal rivers as set by VMRC
species.notes: VMRC recreational table does not print a hickory shad row; only American shad is listed as illegal to possess.

zones.label: Meherrin (below Emporia Dam), Nottoway, Blackwater (Chowan), North Landing and Northwest rivers and tributaries, plus Back Bay
zones.bagNote: 10 per day

zones.label: Chesapeake Bay coastal rivers above and below the fall line
zones.bagNote: As set by VMRC for tidal rivers (no hickory shad rule printed on the VMRC recreational table)

userNotes: Chowan-drainage rivers (Meherrin, Nottoway, Blackwater, North Landing, Northwest) and Back Bay: 10 per day, no size limit.
Chesapeake Bay rivers: DWR defers to VMRC; VMRC's recreational table prints no hickory shad limit, so confirm with VMRC before keeping any.
Do not confuse with American shad, which is catch-and-release only statewide.

species.name: Southern Flounder
species.quote: Southern Flounder - Back Bay and tributaries, including Brinson's Inlet Lake (Lake Tecumseh), and the North Landing River and its tributaries: 6 per day, no fish less than 15 inches
species.notes: DWR rule for Back Bay / North Landing River (inland waters). VMRC does not print a southern flounder row; summer flounder rules apply in VMRC tidal waters.

zones.label: Back Bay and tributaries incl. Lake Tecumseh, and North Landing River and tributaries
zones.bagNote: 6 per day

userNotes: Applies only in Back Bay, Lake Tecumseh and the North Landing River system (DWR waters).
Elsewhere in Virginia tidal waters follow the VMRC summer flounder rule (4 per person; 16 in Jan-May, 17.5 in Jun-Dec).

species.name: Crayfish
species.quote: The possession limit for crayfish is 20 in aggregate. Note: Madtoms, crayfish, and salamanders cannot be bought or sold.
species.notes: Cannot be bought or sold. Rusty, Australian and marbled crayfish are non-native species requiring a permit to possess.

zones.label: Virginia inland waters
zones.bagNote: 20 in aggregate (all species combined)

userNotes: 20 crayfish total per person; they may not be sold.

issues: Could not download any PDF via curl (proxy connect_rejected for webapps.mrc.virginia.gov and dwr.virginia.gov); PDFs were fetched inside the browser tab as base64 and decoded locally with pdftotext - text is verbatim from the PDF layer.

https://mrc.virginia.gov/regulations/fr490.shtm (VMRC shark regulation page linked from the shark ID page) returns 404; shark species lists were taken from the Virginia Administrative Code at law.lis.virginia.gov (4VAC20-490-20 and -40), the regulation the MRC table itself cites.

MRC web table footnote still prints mako size limits (female 83 in / male 71 in FL) although 4VAC20-490-20 (eff. May 1, 2025) and the 2026 card list mako as recreationally prohibited; treated the regulation and 2026 card as authoritative.

The MRC recreational table prints no hickory shad rule; DWR defers Chesapeake-river hickory shad to VMRC. Added Hickory Shad with bag null for Chesapeake rivers and 10/day for the Chowan drainage per DWR; needs VMRC confirmation (4VAC20-530).

DWR Special Regulation Trout Waters and Delayed Harvest pages list ~60 individual stream sections; modeled as rule categories in the Trout correction rather than one zone per stream. The Delayed Harvest page text was truncated at 6,000 chars after the rules paragraph (the rules themselves were captured in full).

The 2026-27 oyster table (4VAC20-720-40) contains obvious typos in the official text ('December January 31, 2027', 'May 32, 2027', 'October 1, 2027, through May 31, 2027'); quoted rows without typos were used.
Lobster: 4VAC20-110 prints size, closed landing period and possession prohibitions but no recreational bag number; bag left null.

Potomac River mainstem and its Virginia tributaries follow Potomac River Fisheries Commission rules (prfc.us) for striped bass and summer flounder; PRFC is not a Virginia agency domain and was not fetched.
Trout Waters page lists 'Trout Fishing Changes & Updates for 2027' - not opened; 2026 rules used.
Striped Bass raw rows 23 and 24 (Chesapeake Bay, Federal waters) have no overlay entries; overlay 22 carries all four zones. Not an error, noted for the data team.
